messages:
Rhea (marketing): Heads-up 1: we need a compact battlecard + webinar blurbs by Monday. Focus: how Redwood beats cloud AI endpoints, LLM APIs, and appliance-style infra. Keep it punchy.
Dev (sales): Field asks: pricing surprises, slow p99s, and vendor lock-in. Want 3 quick one-liners for each objection.
Noah (product): Agreed. My suggested structure: 1) claim, 2) 1-sentence why, 3) 1-line demo talking point.
Priya (eng): Quick perf note so messaging is accurate: in our internal chatbench Redwood's serving stack reduced billed compute by ~1.9x-2.1x on median conversational flows vs a leading cloud endpoint; p50 latency matched; p95 varied by region. Don't promise p99 wins globally yet.
Rhea (marketing): Great. Draft social hero options (short):
  - Option A: "Serve smarter: lower unit costs, predictable latency."
  - Option B: "Keep your models. Cut your inference bills."
  - Option C: "Turn model access into predictable serving economics."
Dev (sales): Option B lands in calls. Short objection/rebut pairings (3 each):
  - Objection: "We're fine on CloudY today."
    Reply: "CloudY is great for prototyping. At scale teams hit opaque bill spikes and tail latency. Redwood adds routing, caching, and predictable pricing controls so SREs and finance can plan."
  - Objection: "We'd have to rework infra to use Redwood."
    Reply: "Redwood's API is drop-in for most workflows; you can keep your model selection and use our routing/caching layer incrementally."
  - Objection: "On-prem infra gives us control."
    Reply: "If you need air-gapped or VPC options we support Private deployments with the same runtime; the win is unified tooling and predictable economics across clouds and on-prem."
Noah (product): Micro-technical lines for the slide (for platform folks):
  "Continuous request coalescing, session KV prefix reuse, and model-variant routing cut repeat compute and keep median latency stable while lowering billed tokens."
Priya (eng): Include a tiny routing example for the demo slide (showing policy + fallbacks):
```json
{
  "policy": "cost-aware",
  "primary_model": "llama-2-70b",
  "fallbacks": ["llama-2-13b-quant","llama-2-13b"],
  "kv_prefix_cache": true,
  "batch_target_ms": 10
}
```
Rhea (marketing): Inbound lead routing rules (simple) for the ops team:
  - Keywords -> AE: "SLA", "compliance", "on-prem", "private", "dedicated"
  - Keywords -> SDR: "trial", "signup", "free credits", "embed", "api key"
  - Lead score >= 80 -> AE outreach, 50-79 -> SDR sequence, <50 -> marketing nurture
  Regex sample: "/\\b(SLA|compliance|on-?prem|private|dedicated)\\b/i"
Dev (sales): Also add demo CTA phrasing: "See routing + fallback in action 1: register for a live slot (limited dedicated capacity demos)"
Priya (eng): For the benchmark slide bullet (one-liner + caveat):
  "Benchmark: median token spend cut ~2x on dialogue workloads vs CloudZ endpoints; demoed in a controlled environment. Numbers vary by prompt shape and region."
Noah (product): OK to ship that as long as we add a tiny footnote: "internal lab results; customer results may vary."
Rhea (marketing): Perfect. I'll assemble a 1-pager, short slide callouts, and a 2-tweet thread for social. Jenkins-bot can you create a marketing asset stub? :sparkles:
jenkins-bot: Created page at https://internal.redwood/marketing/assets/serve-econ-brief (editable by marketing) :white_check_mark:
Dev (sales): I'll add two roleplay snippets to the battlecard once Rhea drops the draft.
Priya (eng): I'll review the technical lines and routing example. If anything changes, I'll post updates here.
Rhea (marketing): Thanks all 1. Aiming to freeze copy Sunday night to hand to design Monday morning.
